Since $2000$ lies between these values,
$$\therefore\ \text{lower estimate } 1.03,\ \text{upper estimate } 1.04$$

4564.stem: A species of rabbit has been introduced to a new environment with an initial population of 200.

parts.latex: If this population experiences growth at a rate of $80\%$ per year what would be the population after 10 years, to the nearest whole number?

After the 10 years the population of rabbits was considered to be in need of management.

If they prevented the growth of the rabbits and reduced the population each year by $20\%$ how many years would it take for the number of rabbits to return to the initial population of 200, to the nearest year.

Show working using the “guess and check” method.

solutions.latex:
Growth of $80\%$ per year gives a multiplier of $1.8$.

$$\begin{aligned} P &= 200(1.8)^n \\ &= 200(1.8)^{10} \\ &= 71409 \end{aligned}$$

meta.marker_note: 0 marks if a linear increase is used.

solutions.latex:
A decrease of $20\%$ per year is compounding, with multiplier $0.8$.

$$P = 71409 \times 0.8^n$$
We need $P = 200$, so test values of $n$.

$$\begin{aligned} n = 26:&\quad 71409 \times 0.8^{26} = 215.82 \\ n = 27:&\quad 71409 \times 0.8^{27} = 172.66 \end{aligned}$$
The population first drops below $200$ at $n=27$; at $n=26$ it is still above $200$.

$$\therefore\ \text{it takes } 27 \text{ years}$$
criteria: Correct answer: compounding decrease formula, guess-and-check shown, 27 years
Correct formula and guess-and-check, or equivalent merit
Correct compounding decrease formula, or equivalent merit

In 2010, 5% of Australia's energy use was solar energy. The percentage of solar energy use has continued to increase exponentially since then.

$$S = 5 \times (1.09)^t$$

solutions.latex:

6048.stem:
A large rechargeable battery has a maximum storage capacity of 40 kWh when new.

After 1 year, the maximum storage capacity is 32 kWh.

The process of decay can be modelled by the function

$$y = ka^t$$

where $y$ is the maximum storage capacity of the battery, in kWh, $t$ years after it starts being used.

parts.latex: What are the values of $k$ and $a$?
Interpret the value of $a$ in this context.

solutions.latex:
When $t = 0$, $y = 40$, so $k = 40$.

When $t = 1$, $y = 32$ and $k = 40$:
$$\begin{aligned} 32 &= 40 \times a^1 \\ a &= \dfrac{32}{40} \\ &= 0.8 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ k = 40,\ a = 0.8$$

Answers could include:

The maximum storage capacity is decreasing at a rate of $20\%$ per year.

Or: $80\%$ of the maximum storage capacity from the previous year remains the following year.

parts.latex: Which graph could represent $y = 4^x$?

solutions.latex:
For $y = 4^x$, when $x = 0$ we get $y = 4^0 = 1$, so the graph cuts the $y$-axis above the origin.

Since $4 > 1$, $y$ increases as $x$ increases, and it increases at an ever faster rate (curving upwards).

Option B decreases, option C is a straight line with negative gradient, and option D is a straight line through the origin, so none of these fits.

The graph in option A is the one that fits, so the answer is option A.

parts.latex: $y = 4^{-x}$ is an example of what relationship?

solutions.latex:
Write the function as $y=4^{-x}=\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^{x}$.

The variable $x$ is in the exponent with a constant base, so this is an exponential relationship.

It is not quadratic or linear, since $x$ is not raised to a power, and it is not reciprocal, which has the form $y=\dfrac{k}{x}$.
$$\therefore\ \text{exponential}$$

6303.stem: A cow has a type of bacteria living in it called a methanogen. The methanogen's population exponentially increases with the equation $P = k(1.2)^t$, where $k$ is a constant, and $t$ is time in years. It is known that after 2 years, there are 288 methanogens in the cow.

parts.latex: Show that the value of $k$ is 200.
After 3 years, what is the population of the methanogens living in the cow?
What is the initial population of the methanogens?
If the population grows over 500, the cow will need to have medical treatment. How many years will it take before the cow requires medical treatment?

solutions.latex:
Substitute $t = 2$ and $P = 288$ into $P = k(1.2)^t$.
$$\begin{aligned} 288 &= k(1.2)^2 \\ k &= \dfrac{288}{1.2^2} \\ &= 200 \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} P &= 200(1.2)^3 \\ &= 345.6 \\ &\approx 346 \end{aligned}$$
$\therefore$ 346 methanogens.

The initial population is at $t = 0$.
$$\begin{aligned} P &= 200(1.2)^0 \\ &= 200 \end{aligned}$$

Use $P = 200(1.2)^n$ and test whole years.
$$\begin{aligned} n = 4:\ P &= 200(1.2)^4 = 414.72 &&(\text{under } 500) \\ n = 5:\ P &= 497.664 &&(\text{under } 500) \\ n = 6:\ P &= 597.1968 &&(\text{over } 500) \end{aligned}$$
Solving $200(1.2)^t=500$ gives $t=\dfrac{\ln 2.5}{\ln 1.2}\approx5.03$.
$$\therefore\ \text{just over } 5 \text{ years (the population passes } 500 \text{ early in the 6th year)}$$

6471.stem:
The population of rabbits in a town is estimated to be 1000 in the year 2000. The population increases by $80\%$ each year. The population of the rabbits after $n$ years is given by

$$P=a^n\times 1000$$

where $P$ is the population of the rabbits and $a$ is a constant.

parts.latex: Find the population of rabbits in the year 2009, correct to three significant figures.

At the end of the year 2009, a disease enters the rabbits’ ecosystem, decreasing the population by $80\%$ each year.

During which year will the rabbit population return to its initial population of 1000?

solutions.latex:
The year 2009 is $n=9$ years after 2000, and $a=1.8$ for an $80\%$ increase.
$$\begin{aligned}P&=1.8^9\times 1000\\&\approx 198\,000\text{ rabbits}\quad\text{(3 sig. fig.)}\end{aligned}$$

A decrease of $80\%$ each year means multiplying by $0.2$. The population $n$ years after 2009 is
$$P=0.2^n\times 198\,000$$
Try values of $n$:
$$\begin{aligned}n=3:&\quad P=1584\\n=4:&\quad P=316.8\end{aligned}$$
The population falls below 1000 in the 4th year after 2009.
$$\therefore\text{ the year 2013}$$
criteria: Uses an appropriate method to find $n$, for example trial and error

6675.stem:
In 2010, the city of Thagoras used the equation $P = A(1.04)^n$ to predict its future population. The city introduced a new policy to slow its population growth and the new equation used was $P = A(b)^n$. In both equations, $P$ is the predicted population and $n$ is the number of years since 2010.

parts.latex: In both equations, $A$ is 3 000 000, what does $A$ represent?
Explain why 1.05 is not a suitable estimate for the value of $b$.
Find the predicted population in 2030 if the new policy had not been introduced.
Given that in the year 2030, the new policy predicts a population of 4 460 000, find the value of $b$ to 2 decimal places.

solutions.latex:
At $n=0$ (the year 2010), $P = A(b)^0 = A$.

$$\therefore\ A \text{ is the population of Thagoras in 2010 (the initial population)}$$

meta.self_check: The graph shows both curves starting at 3 000 000.

solutions.latex:
The original growth factor is $1.04$. The new policy slows population growth, so the new growth factor must be less than $1.04$. A value of $1.05$ is larger than $1.04$ and would make the population grow faster, not slower.

$$\therefore\ 1.05 \text{ is not suitable because } b \text{ must be less than } 1.04$$

meta.self_check: The graph shows the policy curve below the dotted curve.

solutions.latex:
In 2030, $n = 20$. Without the new policy,
$$\begin{aligned} P &= 3\,000\,000\times(1.04)^{20} \\ &\approx 6\,573\,369 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the predicted population is about } 6\,570\,000$$

meta.self_check: Python: 3e6 x 1.04^20 = 6 573 369. Consistent with the dotted curve at n = 20 (about 6.6 million).

criteria: Substitutes correctly and obtains $b^{20}=\dfrac{4.46}{3}$, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: $y = 3^x - 1$ is an example of what relationship?

solutions.latex:
In $y = 3^x - 1$ the variable $x$ is in the index (exponent) with a constant base $3$.

This is the form $y = a^x + c$, which is an exponential relationship, shifted down $1$ unit.

It is not quadratic or linear, since $x$ is not raised to a power, and it is not reciprocal, since $x$ is not in the denominator.

Therefore the answer is option A.

parts.latex:
Jessica aims to run a total distance of 28 kilometres per week. As preparation for an upcoming marathon, she decides to increase the distance by $10\%$ each week.

How many kilometres will she running by the third week?

solutions.latex:
Each week the distance is multiplied by $1.1$.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Week 2} &= 28\times 1.1 = 30.8 \\ \text{Week 3} &= 30.8\times 1.1 = 33.88 \end{aligned}$$
Equivalently, $28\times(1.1)^2=33.88$.
$$\therefore\ \text{She will run } 33.88\text{ km in the third week.}$$

solutions.latex:
Read points from the graph: $(-1,8)$, $(0,4)$, $(1,2)$, with asymptote $y=0$. The values halve as $x$ increases by 1, so the curve is exponential decay with $y$-intercept 4.

Test option C, $y=4(2)^{-x}$:
$$\begin{aligned} x=-1:&\ y=4\times 2=8 \\ x=0:&\ y=4 \\ x=1:&\ y=4\times\dfrac{1}{2}=2 \end{aligned}$$
All three points fit, and $y\to 0$ as $x\to\infty$.

The other options fail: $y=\dfrac{2}{x}$ is undefined at $x=0$; $y=2^{-x}$ gives $y=1$ at $x=0$; $y=2^x+3$ is increasing with asymptote $y=3$.

$$\therefore\ y=4(2)^{-x} \text{ (option C)}$$

parts.latex:
The equation of the following function is in the form $y = a^{x} + b$. Find the values of $a$ and $b$.

\extable{3301_q13_t1}

Graph this function on the below cartesian plane.

\exfigure{3301_q13_1}
What is the asymptote of this graph? (i.e. What value of $y$ does this graph never cross).
Using your graph, or otherwise, estimate the value of $y$ when $x = 0.5$.

solutions.latex:
The function is $y = a^{x} + b$.

When $x = 0$, $y = 2$:

$$\begin{aligned} 2 &= a^{0} + b \\ 2 &= 1 + b \\ b &= 1 \end{aligned}$$

When $x = 1$, $y = 3$:

$$\begin{aligned} 3 &= a^{1} + 1 \\ a &= 2 \end{aligned}$$

The graph of $y = 2^{x} + 1$ passes through $(0, 2)$, $(1, 3)$, $(2, 5)$ and $(3, 9)$, and does not go below $y = 1$.

\exfigure{3301_q13_s1}
criteria: Correct points or correct shape, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex: The graph never goes below $y = 1$, so the asymptote is $y = 1$.

$$\begin{aligned} y &= 2^{0.5} + 1 \\ &\approx 2.4 \end{aligned}$$

Accept $2.1 \le y \le 2.7$.

parts.latex:
The growth of bacteria in a culture can be modelled by the equation: $N = 75(1.05)^t$, where $N$ is the number of bacteria after $t$ hours.

What type of graph would represent this model?

solutions.latex:
The model $N = 75(1.05)^t$ has the form $N = a b^t$, with the variable $t$ in the exponent, $a=75$ and $b=1.05>1$.

This is exponential growth, so the graph is exponential.

A parabola has $t^2$, a line has $t$ to the first power only, and a hyperbola has $t$ in a denominator, so B, C and D are rejected.

Hence the answer is A.
